## Academic profile

I am an interdisciplinary researcher with training in clinical pharmacy and current
expertise in statistical genetics and applied bioinformatics for the analysis of
large-scale genomic and health data. My research focuses on computational and
statistical methods for complex human disease, with particular emphasis on polygenic
modelling, fine-mapping, gene–environment analyses, and reproducible analysis of
large-scale genomic and register-based data. I combine method-oriented quantitative
research with translational interpretation of biological and clinical questions, and
I have active teaching experience in applied data analysis and programming, including
PhD-level instruction in R.

## Background

My path into statistical genetics started in clinical practice. I trained as a
pharmacist (Pharm.D., Isfahan University of Medical Sciences, 2010–2016) and worked
as a clinical pharmacist at Alzahra Hospital while completing a Ph.D. in Clinical
Pharmacy (2016–2023). During that time my interests moved toward the quantitative and
computational side of health research, which led me to a visiting researcher position
at the Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG), Aarhus University, in
2022. I have been based in Aarhus ever since, joining the National Centre for
Register-based Research (NCRR) as a postdoctoral researcher in June 2024. This
background is part of why I care about keeping statistical and computational work
connected to the underlying clinical and biological questions.

## Research interests

- Statistical genetics and computational genomics
- Bioinformatics and applied computational biology
- Polygenic modelling and fine-mapping
- Gene–environment analyses and family-based designs
- Psychiatric genetics and complex disease biology
- Register-based and longitudinal health data analysis
- Reproducible computational workflows and high-performance computing

## Methodological expertise

- Genome-wide association studies (GWAS)
- Polygenic score analysis
- Bayesian linear regression and fine-mapping
- Integration of genomic and register-based data
- Reproducible analysis pipelines in R
- Statistical genetics and risk modelling for complex disorders

## Teaching

I am course developer, course leader, and instructor for **Basic R** (PhD level) at
Aarhus University — responsible for course design, teaching materials, and delivery.
The course was first offered in 2026, with deliveries in April and December. I also
lead and teach **Advanced R** (PhD level), an established PhD course at Aarhus
University, from 2026.

I completed the University Pedagogical Programme at Aarhus University in spring 2026.

Earlier in my career I was a teaching assistant in Clinical Pharmacy Practice and
Community Pharmacy Practice at Isfahan University of Medical Sciences (2017–2021).

## Supervision and mentoring

I am currently co-supervising three PhD research projects in statistical genetics and
epidemiology at Aarhus University. Previously, I co-supervised five PharmD and PhD
projects on drug safety, dialysis outcomes, and depression in diabetes.

## Honors and service

I received the European Society of Human Genetics (ESHG) Fellowship for European
Countries in 2025, and was nominated for the ESHG Best Poster Award the same year. In
2020, I ranked first in the Clinical Pharmacy Board Examination.

I regularly review for journals spanning genetics and pharmacy practice, including
*Brain Communications*, *Scientific Reports*, and the *Journal of Research in Pharmacy
Practice*, and I contribute to academic organisation and collaborative research
activities within the Aarhus University research environment.

For the complete, dated record of appointments, education, teaching, and service, see
my [CV](cv.qmd). For my papers and preprints, see [Publications](publications.qmd).
